claude.label: Claude
claude.research_note: Headless `claude -p` has WebSearch/WebFetch available, so it can do live evidence research for the grounding layer (settings.research_enabled). Extra fields here are informational only — runAgent reads just command/args/input/env_required.
claude.model_note: Cairn passes NO --model unless the person picks one in Settings -> Agents (Everyday = the fast class, Deep work = the deep class; settings.model_class_bindings). The CLI then runs whatever model the account's plan gives it — a lower plan cannot run every alias, and `--model fable` there exits within a second. model_choices are the dropdown's offered ALIASES, never dated IDs: the installed CLI resolves each alias to the newest model of that family, so the list keeps up with model releases without a code change (claude 2.1.294 --help: "Provide an alias for the latest model (e.g. 'fable', 'opus', or 'sonnet') or a model's full name"). claude has no non-interactive model-listing command (2.1.294: no models subcommand), so models_list stays null and the curated aliases plus a free-text 'Other' are the choices. A chosen alias the account cannot use falls back to the CLI default (runWithModelAccessFallback, src/agentModelPins.ts).

read_tools.note: Verified live 2026-11-11 against a throwaway loopback MCP server: --mcp-config with ONE http server + --strict-mcp-config (no ambient MCP server can widen it) + --tools "" (no built-in tool at all) + --allowedTools naming only the mcp__cairn-coach-read__<tool> reads + --setting-sources "" (no user/project settings, hooks or permissions; the OAuth login still works). One tools/call, the correct answer, ~3 s wall; told to read a local file it answered that the session has no file or shell tools, and still answered. Tool names reach the model as mcp__cairn-coach-read__<tool>. These args carry the confinement themselves: {no_tools_args} never expands when MCP args are passed — which is also why the last two flags are repeated here from no_tools_args: --disable-slash-commands, and --no-session-persistence, without which every native turn would leave a session JSONL holding the prompt and every health read under ~/.claude/projects. Streams as before: stream-json emits tool_use/tool_result as assistant/user events and input_json_delta deltas, none of which streamDelta reads as text.

structured_output.note: claude 2.1.220 --help: '--json-schema <schema>  JSON Schema for structured output validation.' Verified live (re-verified on 2.1.258, 2026-09-02): stdout is the bare payload with no envelope, so extractJson is unchanged. A top-level anyOf is REJECTED (API 400: input_schema.type required) — schemas must be a single top-level object.

install.size_note: npm 2026-11-11: @anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64@2.1.322 unpacks to 341.9 MB (arm64 341.5 MB); the launcher package is 0.2 MB. 2.1.322 is the build the native coach-read attach (read_tools) was verified on. npm's cache lives in a deleted temp dir, not on the data volume.

codex.description: OpenAI Codex (Sign in with ChatGPT). Auth: ~/.codex.
codex.label: ChatGPT

read_tools.note: Verified live 2026-11-11 (codex exec against a throwaway loopback MCP server): 7/7 correct, median 7 s. Without default_tools_approval_mode=approve the call fails ('MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never'). --disable shell_tool is MANDATORY: with the shell left on it read a local file. --ignore-user-config keeps an ambient MCP server from ~/.codex/config.toml out of the run (auth still comes from CODEX_HOME; a model set only in config.toml is not read on these runs — a Settings model binding still is, through {model_args}). NOT a strict allowlist: apply_patch and connector tools remain, held by the --sandbox read-only already in args — hence confinement 'sandboxed'. The probe ran with --json to watch the item.started/completed mcp_tool_call events; Cairn's runs do NOT pass --json, so stdout stays the final agent message and the existing parse path (and --output-schema) is unchanged — the listener records every call server-side instead. Codex has no streaming here, so it answers one-shot. A feature name a later CLI drops fails the spawn, which the chat path treats as an attach failure and retries once on the prompt loop.

structured_output.note: codex 0.145.0 `exec --help`: '--output-schema <FILE>  Path to a JSON Schema file describing the model's final response shape'. It takes a PATH, not inline JSON, so runAgentImpl writes a 0600 temp file per run and unlinks it on close. Verified live under --sandbox read-only: the final agent message is the bare payload (the banner it precedes carries no braces, so extractJson still anchors correctly). Only valid on the `exec` subcommand.

codex.model_note: No curated model_choices: codex model names are versioned (gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-6-sol…), not aliases, so a curated list would date itself. Instead the Settings dropdown reads the CLI's own catalog: `codex debug models` (verified on codex-cli 0.160.0, 2026-10-08: non-interactive, prints {models:[{slug, visibility, …}]} as JSON, ~650 KB, refreshed from the account's catalog with the bundled one as its fallback) — models_format codex_json keeps only listed (visibility != hide) slugs. With nothing chosen codex runs on its own configured model and Cairn only sets effort. Consequence: 'max' is declared per-model in the CLI's own catalog (gpt-5.6-* accept it; gpt-5.5 and older top out at xhigh), so a codex that resolves an older model rejects 'max' at request time, not config-parse time. Nothing in TASK_EXECUTION_PROFILES requests 'max', so this is reachable only via a user profile binding.

antigravity.description: Google Antigravity CLI 'agy' (the successor to the Gemini CLI; Google account). Auth: ~/.gemini.
antigravity.label: Google
antigravity.login_note: Print mode, not the TUI. Verified on agy 1.3.1 (2026-10-07, in the container): signed out, `agy -p /quota` prints 'Authentication required. Please visit the URL to log in:' and the WHOLE Google OAuth URL (…&response_type=code&scope=…&state=…) on ONE line, then 'Waiting for authentication (timeout 60s)...' / 'Or, paste the authorization code here and press Enter:' — no menu choice first. Pasting the code + Enter signs in, answers the /quota slash command (no agent turn, no quota spent) and exits 0: that exit IS the success signal. Unanswered, it ends after the fixed 60s ('Error: authentication interrupted.' / 'error: authentication failed or timed out' + a status:ERROR envelope) and exits non-zero; no flag extends that wait (`agy --help`), so the panel spawns this only when the person taps Open, and a timeout offers a fresh link (a new process, a new URL; the old code is dead). Bare interactive `agy` was the previous sign-in and is unusable on a phone: it opens with a numbered menu, and its TUI hard-wraps the OAuth URL to the PTY width inside a scroll window, so a 40-column screen yielded a cut URL (Google: 'Required parameter is missing: response_type'). agy 1.3.1 has no login/auth subcommand.
antigravity.status_note: Re-verified signed-OUT on agy 1.3.1 (2026-10-07): the probe no longer fails fast — it prints 'Authentication required. Please visit the URL to log in:' plus a Google OAuth URL on stdout and then WAITS up to 60s for a pasted code, so a short spawn timeout ends it with that text already on stdout (parse it as signed out; never as undetectable). agy 1.1.24: `-p /quota --output-format json` answers WITHOUT an agent turn (no quota spent, no conversation left behind) and returns {status:'SUCCESS', command:{name:'usage', data:{groups:[{buckets:[{window:'weekly'|'5h', remaining_fraction, reset_time}]}]}}} — a signed-in banner AND the live limit state in one probe. Parsed by parseStatusOutput/parseAgyQuota in src/agents.ts. `agy models` (the previous probe) fetched the catalog over the network on every boot and said nothing about quota.
antigravity.auth_state_note: Deliberately empty: agy creates ~/.gemini (config/, antigravity-cli/) on ANY run, the signed-out status probe included (verified on 1.3.1 in an empty HOME), so the directory proves nothing. agy keeps its token in the OS keyring (Google's docs) and, without one, in a fallback store whose path is not documented; until that file is verified on a container, the /quota probe is the only evidence.
antigravity.model_effort_suffix_note: agy accepts both an alias plus --effort (`--model gemini-4-argon --effort high`) and a name with the effort baked in (`gemini-4-argon-low`), but refuses the two together ('--model gemini-4-argon-low conflicts with --effort', verified 2026-10-16). Bind the bare alias so server effort policy applies; a suffixed name runs WITHOUT --effort (resolveAgentExecutionProfile, src/agents.ts).
antigravity.settings_note: Every coaching run passes --settings '{"permissions":{"deny":["command(*)"]}}' (both arg lists). Verified live 2026-11-11 on agy 1.5.5: without the explicit deny a headless shell attempt blanks the WHOLE reply (response:"", 'no output produced — a tool required the "command" permission…', which Cairn classifies permission_denied; seen live that day); with it the denial is an ordinary tool error and the model still answers. It composes with {file_access_args} (--add-dir) and with the read_url(*) grant ensureAntigravityHeadlessPermissions keeps in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json.

read_tools.note: No per-run or project MCP attach exists (2026-11-11): --settings rejects mcpServers, and only the user-level config takes a server — attaching there would widen every agy run, so agy stays on the prompt loop. ~15 s per answer when probed.

structured_output.note: agy 1.1.8 gained what 1.1.7 had none of: '--json-schema  Optional JSON schema string or path to a schema file to enforce structured output'. Unlike grok it does NOT imply the output format — `agy -p … --json-schema …` alone exits with '--json-schema can only be used when --output-format is json or stream-json', so the format flag is part of this template rather than a separate slot. Verified live on 1.1.8: with both flags stdout is a telemetry ENVELOPE — {conversation_id, status, response, duration_seconds, num_turns, structured_output, json_schema, usage} — so the first `{` is NOT the contract. `structured_output` carries the parsed payload and `response` the same payload as a string, hence the envelope declaration; without it an op would receive the telemetry object. Both flags ride the {schema_args} slot, so a run with no RunOpts.schema still gets plain text and the prose contract + extractJson path.

install.note: Pinned to Google's own release manifest (https://antigravity-cli-auto-updater-974169037036.us-central1.run.app/manifests/<platform>.json with <platform> = linux_amd64 | linux_arm64 | darwin_arm64 | darwin_amd64, as install.sh names them; read 2026-11-11 → 1.5.6, each tarball downloaded and its SHA-512 checked against the manifest; linux-x64 unpacks to 279.5 MB, linux-arm64 262.5 MB). 1.5.6 is at or past 1.5.5, where the --settings command(*) deny on every agy run was verified. The pins are each platform's versioned GCS tarball and the SHA-512 that manifest publishes for it. install.sh itself is MUTABLE — it is a bootstrapper that reads that same manifest, downloads the tarball, checks its SHA-512 and copies `antigravity` to ~/.local/bin/agy — so pinning the script's own sha256 bricked setup the day Google edited it (ee1ea43c… → 62966c07…). A versioned tarball never changes under its URL, so its pin cannot go stale; when Google prunes it, or no pin fits the host (musl), scripts/install-agent-cli.mjs runs install.sh fetched over HTTPS from antigravity.google instead. Once installed, `agy update` (and agy's own background self-update) keeps it current.

grok.description: xAI Grok Build (SuperGrok/X Premium+). Headless may need XAI_API_KEY.
grok.label: Grok
grok.login_note: Re-verified on grok 1.0.46 (2026-10-07): `grok login --device-auth` (alias --device-code) still exists and needs no TTY. It prints 'To sign in, open this URL in your browser:' + https://accounts.x.ai/oauth2/device?user_code=XXXX-XXXX, then 'Confirm this code in your browser:' + the bare code, then waits ('Waiting for authorization...'). Tokens land in ~/.grok/auth.json.
grok.status_note: CHANGED on grok 1.0.46 (2026-10-07): signed OUT, `grok models` exits 0 and prints 'You are not authenticated.' ABOVE 'Default model: …' and 'Available models:' — so 'Available models:' alone is no longer a signed-in signal; 'You are not authenticated' must be read first, as signed out. grok 1.0.13 has login/logout but no status subcommand. `grok models` is the cheapest authenticated call: signed in it prints 'Available models:' (and 'You are using XAI_API_KEY.' when the env key is the credential), so that banner is the positive signal; anything else falls through to auth_state (~/.grok/auth.json from the in-app device-auth login).

read_tools.note: Native MCP works (2026-11-11: 5/5, ~7 s) through a PROJECT ./.grok/config.toml in the run cwd ([mcp_servers.<name>] url = …) plus --trust --permission-mode dontAsk --allow 'mcp__<name>__*' --tools use_tool,search_tool --disable-web-search --max-turns 8 — but the folder must be trusted (writes ~/.grok/trusted_folders.toml), and any ambient user-level MCP server leaks into the run unless denied by name (one reached a shell). So NOT enabled in this phase: grok stays on the prompt loop. A later phase can enable it inside the container, where the home config is Cairn's own.

structured_output.note: grok 0.2.114 --help: '--json-schema <SCHEMA>  JSON Schema for structured output. When set, the model is constrained to produce JSON matching this schema. Implies --output-format json.' That implied switch is why `envelope` exists: verified live, stdout becomes {text, thought, usage, …, structuredOutput} — the first `{` is the ENVELOPE, so without unwrapping, extractJson would hand the op a telemetry object (and `thought` would drag raw reasoning into it). Deliberately absent from `stream.args`: --json-schema would override --output-format streaming-json. Re-verified live on grok 1.0.13 (2026-09-02, a major bump): `-p` is now `-p, --single <PROMPT>`, `--cwd`, `--json-schema`, `--reasoning-effort` (alias --effort) and `-m/--model` all still exist; the json envelope keys {text, thought, structuredOutput} are unchanged; `--output-format` offers plain|json|streaming-json|streaming-messages-json and streaming-json still emits {type:"text"|"thought", data} lines, so the stream adapter in src/agents.ts is unchanged. Vendor `update` writes to ~/.grok/bin; scripts/install-agent-cli.mjs persists the newest build to .cairn-tools/bin.

install.note: xAI publishes no checksums, so these sha256 pins are Cairn's own, taken 2026-11-03 from the versioned builds install.sh resolves (https://x.ai/cli/stable → 1.0.70; grok-<version>-<os>-<arch>[.gz|.zst], the .gz unpacking to the same binary as the raw file). install.sh is a bootstrapper that verifies nothing beyond the binary running `--version`; it is mutable, so it is only the fallback for a pruned pin (xAI does prune: 0.2.93 is a 404, 1.0.13 still serves) or an unpinned host, fetched over HTTPS from x.ai. `grok update` keeps an installed CLI current.
